contexts.text: In general, the origins of diseases are intemperance, etc. SE 4592.
With luxury and intemperance... it is the same.
Intemperance (a really weighty cause of concubinage).

When I had taken... much milk and bread... the Spirits kept their senses in intemperance, of which they accused me. Hence from the dry things there arose an odour of human ordure, and from the liquids a foul odour of urine, which adhered to my nostrils... because they kept their senses in such intemperance.
By eating, in these passages, is meant luxury and intemperance...
When intemperance is removed, temperance enters.
5. a. The opposites which destroy charity, and relate to... intemperance, etc.
